To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anticonvulsants benzodiazepenes act by allosterically modulating the chloride ionophoric action of gamma-aminobutryric acid (GABA).
benzodiazepinergic drugs modulate the chloride ionophores of mammalian brain through the GABA receptor, and that the benzodiazapine receptor is an allosteric site on the GABA receptor.
the benzodiazepam receptor is allosterically coupled, through gamma-aminobutryic acid, to the chloride ionophor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism by which the benzodiazepamines exert their anticonvulsent action.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of the benzodiazapines, a group of anticonvulsants which are widely used clinically for the management of anxiety and epilepsy.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of benzodiazepene-induced seizure control, and with the identification of the molecular target for benzodiazepenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
benzodiazepinones exert their anticonvulsants effects through an action on the GABA-Cl- receptor-chloride ionophore complex.
the benzodiazapines are allosteric modulators of a gamma-aminobutryic acid receptor complex that is associated with the chloride ionophores of the postsynaptic membrane of the central nervous system.
benzodiazepenes exert their anticonvulsive action by enhancing gamma-aminobutric acid-mediated inhibition of neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benzodiazapines act as positive modulators of the gamma-aminoburytic acid receptor-chloride channel complex.
the benzodiazapines exert their anticonvulsan action through an interaction with the gamma-aminobutyratc acid receptor complex.
the anticonvulsants act by increasing the affinity of the chloride ion channel for chloride ions, thereby decreasing the rate of chloride ion efflux.
The main takeaway from our work is that
benzodiazepenes act by modulating the GABA receptor complex.
the benzodiazapines act on a chloride ionophore that requires gamma-aminobuteric acid for its activity.
